rows: A harvestman has a single pair of eyes, set back to back on a small turret in the middle of its body. Each eye looks out to one side.
A harvestman's eyes probably give only a rough picture of light and dark. A large dark object makes a species of Leiobunum flee, and in the laboratory harvestmen move away from light.
The most photographed harvestman, Phalangium opilio, also carries two more pairs of eyes inside its body, both shrunk to traces. They may help set its daily clock.
In two cave harvestmen from New Zealand the eyes respond to ultraviolet, blue and green light, over a range of brightness of at least a hundred thousand to one.
Harvestmen find food, mates and enemies mostly by touching and tasting them with their first pair of legs and their palps, and they sense little from a distance.

No one has measured how much detail a harvestman sees. This view assumes coarse sight of a few large shapes, grey, clearest out to each side. The dim seam's width, and the buzz at a knock (&draw=buzz), are the app's.
The touch and taste of a harvestman's legs and palps carry most of what it knows, and the camera records neither.

rows.title: Eyes
rows.text: Many harvestmen, but not all, have a pair of eyes with a lens in the hard outer layer of the body, set on a small tower in the middle of the back. If you are a European harvestman, the abstract of a review of gene-expression work describes that visible pair, plus a hidden inner pair of side eyes and a second hidden pair of median eyes. For other harvestmen nobody has recorded how many eyes you have or what kind they are, and nobody has measured how well you see.
rows.note: R1's value is cut off, so I used only the pairs its quote and value name. I did not total the eyes.

rows.title: Rough images
rows.text: If you are a Heteromitobates discolor guarding your eggs, you use your eyes to find your way back to your clutch, and with your eyes painted over you steer by sensing your own movements instead. A large dark object made a Leiobunum harvestman run away. Nobody has measured how sharply you see or what shapes you can tell apart.
rows.note: Left out R3 (negative phototaxis, night activity) to stay within three sentences; its quote is truncated.

rows.title: Hidden eyes
rows.text: One pair of your eyes is easy to spot, and two more pairs are hidden. If you are a European harvestman, a review of gene-expression work found that one hidden pair is a lateral pair, shrunken and moved inside your body, and the other is an extra pair of median eyes that is just as cryptic.
rows.note: R1 is an abstract and its value text is cut off, so the row gives no total count and says nothing about what the hidden eyes sense.

rows.title: Color and dim light
rows.text: If you are the harvestman Megalopsalis tumida, your eyes sense ultraviolet best, with a second broad peak from blue to green, and they respond across at least 5 log units of light intensity, a hundred-thousandfold range. Ultraviolet is light that humans cannot see at all. If you are any other harvestman, nobody has measured which colors you sense or how dim a light you can use.
rows.note: Only Megalopsalis tumida is measured. I dropped the year and the word "report", and left out the phototaxis claim because the R2 value text is cut off.

rows.title: Touch and taste
rows.text: A harvestman called Iporangaia pustulosa noticed live isopods only when it touched them, mostly with its first pair of legs, according to the abstract of one study. Another, Discocyrtus pectinifemur, detects the smell of fresh dead prey through a mesh and stays near it. Nobody has measured how you sense touch or taste, so neither result is known to be yours.
rows.note: Both records come from other harvestman species, so the row stays grade i. No record covers taste by contact, so the row gives smell only for the second species.

rows.title: Sharpness and field
rows.text: Nobody has measured how sharply you see, or how wide an area your eyes take in at once. Your two eyes sit together on a small raised bump on top of your body, and no one has tested what they can make out.
rows.note: No records were provided, so I cited none and stated no numbers. The sentence about two eyes on a raised bump is general harvestman anatomy with no record behind it, so please confirm or remove it.
